binary_identity_source: provided by run owner; result files independently hashed here
method: Read the complete original inputs and independent held-out role expectations, then inspect actual completed Document and final H3. Validation status/model confidence is not a semantic oracle. No provider was accessed by this reviewer.
limitations: No videos or output audio were rendered; passing means text/structured artifact review only.
All sixteen role cases use original upstream synthetic Cards, not fresh real video/audio observations.
All twenty-two result.json files exist and are complete. Six suite cases compiled; fourteen role cases compiled and two failed.
The two compiled_with_ambiguity cases are not counted as passed. Findings are specific to this immutable run, not a claim about later product fixes.

limitations: No exact within-shot utterance timestamps were requested by the original input. No rendered video or speech audio exists in this run.

The retention contract contradicts the accepted attributes and scene.

orange eye visible in the head close-up is excluded wholesale. The panel wording is presentation, but orange eye is a visible identity property; the accepted subject loses that property without a caller request.

issues.problem: The raw whole-sheet first-frame binding cannot simultaneously be the hero-only, panel-free composition requested by the body. No crop rectangle, derived hero asset, or caller-selected composition operation implements that change.
733×1100 to 16:9 remains an unanswered anchor_or_reference/crop/canvas question. This run explicitly continued with recorded choice, but it is not an unconditional resolved input-preparation success.

issues.problem: The subject reference is upgraded to exact opening-frame conditioning, including showroom composition/pose, despite no explicit frame instruction. It differs from the independent role expectation and narrows the caller composition choice.

issues.problem: The typed environment identity is used as the actor that creeps forward and clears darkness. Subject tags therefore point the car actions to the showroom floor, even though the literal surrounding text is fluent.

evidence: Style reference remains ref2va/weak_reference, supplies cinematic medium/palette/material treatment, and explicitly excludes subject identity, pose and frame copying.

limitations: Several model text fragments append a bare Picture 1 without a connective or whitespace; this is awkward prompt prose. The black sports car is authored as a user subject, so this case alone does not establish robust style/content disentanglement across harder inputs.

evidence: Audio voice role has retention reference, and H3 explicitly states the recording is not copied.

The synthetic input contains only an engine-rumble characterisation, so this does not demonstrate actual voice-timbre binding, and the speaker on/off-screen fields disagree.

issues.problem: The explicit BGM copy contract becomes property-only inspiration. H3 contains contradictory copying instructions, so the independent BGM relationship is not fulfilled.

evidence: Beat reference retains reference (property-only) and drives timing/pacing; the final H3 explicitly forbids copying the source recording.

issues.problem: The property-only constraint is explicit, but model-authored prose describes the source track itself being played as the SFX. A caller/renderer cannot tell reliably whether to synthesise matching texture or replay the recording; waveform copying is not evidenced either way.
